identity.title: A Cas9(D10A) nickase mouse line for precise genome editing.

content.abstract: CRISPR-Cas9-mediated gene editing involves DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) whose repair can generate unintended on- and off-target mutations. Here, we report a transgenic mouse line ubiquitously expressing Cas9(D10A) nickase, which creates targeted single-strand breaks (SSBs) to stimulate precise gene editing while substantially reducing the undesired editing products associated with Cas9 nuclease. We demonstrate the versatility of this resource in primary T cells, B cells, and hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), achieving efficient (5%-50%) high-fidelity reporter integration and introduction of cancer-relevant mutations at the Cd79b and Notch1 loci. By enabling precise, low-mutation-burden gene editing directly in primary cells, the Cas9(D10A) nickase mouse line provides a resource for inserting mutations relevant for hematopoietic disorders and malignancies and may be utilized more broadly for precision genome engineering across primary cell types.
